observations.summary: Private447 differs from 20d94ec in content only at the three paths, but git diff also reports a mode-only change on tools/typescript-boundary/bin/check-boundary.mjs. Integrate by copying exactly the three paths; confirm the product diff has no mode change. SHA pins do not bind mode.

No test proves native work is not started before the charge/spend (M08/M09 survive); the test name overclaims. Route wrappers through an injectable _in function like account.rs and assert a panicking syscall/resolver is unreachable on budget refusal.

The 128-entry bound is the sole guard for a well-formed 129-entry directory response (3240 <= 3244 B) and is untested (M10); without it entry(128) would panic. Add 129-entry directory and file fixtures.
acl_flags() never asserted (M03); omitted-with-data test mutates only length (M12); resolve_native kind mapping untested beyond User (M13); cost assertions are tautological to the formula (M11).
Native assertion matches!(NotReturned | Entries(_) | NoAclSentinel) enumerates every variant and cannot fail; assert per-state accessor consistency instead.
decode/resolve/quad and three constants are not cfg-gated like directory_birth.rs helpers; by inspection Linux non-test builds would warn dead_code. Linux not replayed (no Linux std installed).
entry(i) returns None for omission, sentinel and out-of-range alike; the later access-exclusion predicate must be state-first and review must refuse a predicate built on entry() alone.
Filesec header owner/group GUIDs neither validated nor exposed; raw ACE UUIDs retained privately but not exposed, so distinct Unresolved principals are indistinguishable. Not rights or flags.
Nits: descriptor_acl_capture_cost could be pub const fn; mod declaration placed after a test module; BUFFER_BYTES derivation (probe CAP 128+44+128*24) undocumented.
Strict Clippy -D warnings fails on pre-existing, byte-identical work_ledger.rs new_without_default (deliberate no-Default design); with only that lint allowed Clippy passes, including the new module.
